stories.title: Actual native harness adapter and independent roles
stories.journey: The main agent uses real harness-native worker/test-author/verifier/integrator APIs with explicit capabilities and no simulated workers.
tests: A real authorized harness delegates and collects an owned-file implementation candidate.
Unavailable native concurrency is reported and bounded, not replaced by twenty heavyweight CLI processes.
Implementer cannot write frozen tests, controller state, pins, security policy or another lane.
Test author/verifier identity and actual test commands are distinct from implementation self-reports.
Adapter shutdown cancels/joins all owned work and never invents credentials or extra budget.

stories.title: Rolling twenty-worker scheduling without batch barriers
stories.journey: Maintain a target of twenty safe ready workers and refill freed execution slots while independent verification/integration continues.
tests: Start twenty independent ready workers when harness and resource budgets permit.
Completing one worker starts another before the slowest original worker finishes.
Ready work with satisfied dependencies is admitted as soon as integrated proof becomes available.
Backpressure and actual harness/provider limits reduce occupancy honestly without exceeding configured caps.
No ready work with pending/blocked tasks returns an incomplete result, not a project-completed claim.

stories.title: Durable one-file child tasks and path ownership
stories.journey: Split vertical parents into explicit one-file children, prewire shared contracts and reserve path/subtree ownership across local and fork repositories.
tests: Two different task IDs cannot concurrently write the same path or overlapping subtree.
Child task output outside its one-file grant is rejected before acceptance.
Shared schemas/routes/manifests/migrations are changed only by the serialized integrator.
Parent completion requires every required child on the current integrated revision.
New discovery children inherit requirements/tests and survive controller restart without disappearing from scope.

stories.title: Trusted frozen-test evidence and zero-test rejection
stories.journey: Independently author/run behavioral RED, freeze commands/tests, verify GREEN and reject source-presence or worker-report substitutes.
tests: Real compiling failing test is captured before implementation with exact test/command hashes.
Changed frozen tests, zero discovered tests, ignored suites and missing artifacts fail closed.
Worker-generated PASS text and edited status flags cannot produce accepted evidence.
Denial/cancellation tests assert absent effects and reclaimed resources.
Verifier runs outside implementer write authority and emits bounded redacted evidence tied to candidate revision.

stories.title: Serialized integration before acceptance and dependency release
stories.journey: Integrate each verified candidate against current mainline, resolve additive changes safely, rerun affected tests and only then accept/unlock dependents.
tests: Merge/rebase failure leaves task unaccepted and dependents blocked.
A clean worktree containing unintegrated precommitted branch changes is not treated as a no-op success.
Diverged nonconflicting candidates integrate serially without discarding either contribution.
Post-integration test failure prevents acceptance even when candidate verification passed.
Acceptance records identify exact integrated revision, frozen test hashes and successful rerun atomically.

stories.title: Crash-safe leases, fencing, receipts and recovery
stories.journey: Persist ownership and append-only evidence with fencing tokens through execution, verification and integration, and safely recover interrupted work.
tests: Heartbeat continues for completed workers waiting on verification/integration.
Expired or stale owners cannot write/release a newly assigned lease.
Crash during acceptance publication does not produce accepted-but-unintegrated state.
Two controller starts cannot both acquire the singleton through a check-then-write race.
Recovery proves prior work stopped, preserves evidence and avoids duplicate ambiguous side effects.

stories.title: Provider, RAM, validation and retry budget enforcement
stories.journey: Keep high delegation concurrency while allowing only one heavy validation and respecting actual provider/RAM/cost constraints.
tests: Twenty logical workers do not start twenty Cargo/browser/full-workspace validation processes.
Measured memory pressure stops admission while preserving OS reserve and in-flight cleanup.
Provider account concurrency/rate/cost limits and Retry-After are honored without limit evasion.
Repairable failures retry at most three times; auth/security/signing/budget failures block immediately.
Logs, pending integrations and output are bounded; shutdown reclaims all resources.

stories.title: Reconcile old controller and all completion entrypoints
stories.journey: Remove the old accepted-before-integration and batch/lease gaps, reconcile missing prefix/dependency semantics and make all approved launchers consume the full scope.
tests: Legacy accepted flags and flat prd exports cannot bypass new release evidence.
Adding explicit dependencies does not silently remove required legacy dependency protection.
Every legacy/new task family loads, cycles/missing dependencies fail and discovered work remains visible.
Old and new controller entrypoints either enforce the same trusted policy or clearly refuse unsafe execution.
Full existing bootstrap/canonical guards remain enabled and pass without weakening frozen assertions.

stories.title: Reproducible platform artifacts and signed distribution
stories.journey: Produce reproducible supported Linux/macOS/Windows artifacts with integrity, provenance and platform signing where required.
tests: Clean builders compile the pinned native app and bundle required assets/libraries.
Artifact checksum/SBOM/license/provenance identify exact source and toolchain inputs.
macOS notarization and Windows signing use actual authorized identities or remain blocked.
Wrong architecture/corrupted downloads are rejected by installation.
Upgrades preserve data and a failed release can be rolled back without silent schema loss.

stories.title: Clean-machine local installed acceptance matrix
stories.journey: Prove the end-user install/start/use journey on clean supported systems rather than development-only cargo invocations.
tests: Install then type opencode2 with no manual serve/database/session setup on each supported target.
Only release artifacts are present; Node/Bun/Cargo/Zig/development web servers are absent.
Provider fixture drives actual edit/approval/stream/persistence and restart/resume.
Two terminal clients share one authenticated daemon and correct workspace state.
Record terminal/process/artifact evidence and honest unsupported platform results.

stories.title: Authorized live-provider canary evidence
stories.journey: Complement deterministic protocol fixtures with explicit budgeted live checks against authorized supported providers.
tests: At least the declared supported provider protocols complete an actual small coding turn.
Usage/cache/effort/tool behavior is compared to real provider responses without fabricated metrics.
Rate/auth/model errors produce actionable UI states and respect provider policy.
Canary inputs use disposable data and reports contain no secrets.
Missing credentials or budget yields blocked/skipped-without-acceptance, never a fake live pass.

stories.title: Full legacy and source-parity release proof
stories.journey: Re-run every required old/new product scenario and source coverage on the integrated release tree.
tests: Every legacy ID and original requirement remains represented in the evidence set.
All required source surfaces have test mappings and documented verified behavior.
Accepted-but-unwired code, TBD descriptions and missing evidence prevent certification.
Changes after a passing candidate invalidate stale revision-specific proof.
No optional-runtime flag removes a mandatory full-release feature from accounting.

stories.title: Hosted and real mobile release proof
stories.journey: Verify the owned staging deployment and installed iOS/Android apps with real paired PCs through the named tunnel.
tests: One account controls multiple paired PCs and session tabs from both real platforms.
Real remote approval, file edit, stream and interruption agree with local state.
Sleep/background/network/tunnel restart and revoked devices have correct recoverable outcomes.
Staging ingress/auth/isolation checks demonstrate no unauthenticated origin/PTY access.
Signed builds, device/OS versions and exact PC/gateway/tunnel evidence are preserved; mocks are insufficient.

stories.title: Whole-application resource, security and soak acceptance
stories.journey: Measure the complete app and supported isolation backends under long sessions, many clients/agents and failure injection.
tests: Startup/RSS/idle CPU/frame/latency/disk measurements include all children and optional hosts.
Large history, stream floods, repeated reconnect and cancellation stay within configured bounds.
Real OS secret/path/process isolation survives adversarial tool/plugin inputs.
Disabled features have no hidden background runtime/connection costs.
Run crash/restart/backup/retention soak with no unbounded leak or silent history deletion.

stories.title: User setup, pair/connect and recovery documentation
stories.journey: Document verified install, first-run, account pairing, phone use, service control and recovery separately from contributor build steps.
tests: A fresh-user walkthrough follows only install and opencode2 plus in-app consent.
Pair/connect and phone account steps match actual UI and security scope.
Operator self-host/tunnel instructions distinguish one-time deployment from every-user setup.
Supported platforms, compatibility hosts and feature limitations match runtime capability reports.
Troubleshooting uses redacted diagnostics and never asks users to expose credentials or mutate original history.

stories.title: Independent full-product completion decision
stories.journey: The trusted verifier issues completion only when the entire legacy/additive/discovered scope has integrated-revision proof and every required release journey passes.
tests: Missing task, source surface, test obligation, platform or device evidence fails closed.
Worker self-report, zero-test success and fabricated/untrusted receipt files cannot grant acceptance.
Every proof binds tested commit, frozen suite, command, positive counts and hashed artifacts.
Unintegrated branches, failed post-merge tests or changed source invalidate completion.
No-ready-work with pending/blocked tasks reports exact blockers and never says all tasks are complete.
